{{Short description|American biostatistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2023}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=April 2023}}
'''Lisa Anderson Weissfeld''' is an American [[Biostatistics|biostatistician]] whose publications include work on the risks, prognoses, and treatment outcomes for [[pneumonia]], [[sepsis]], and [[end-of-life care]]; she is one of the authors of the [[pneumonia severity index]]. She has also published [[basic research]] on sparse data in [[meta-analysis]], on [[multicollinearity]], and on the dichotomization of [[ordinal data]], and is one of the namesakes of the Wei–Lin–Weissfeld model in [[recurrent event analysis]].{{r|wlw|wlw2}} She worked for many years as a professor at the [[University of Pittsburgh]].

==Education and career==
Weissfeld earned a Ph.D. in 1982 at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], with the dissertation ''Bounds on the Efficiencies of Commonly Used Nonparametric Statistics'' supervised by Sam Wieand.{{r|mg}} She became a professor of biostatistics at the University of Pittsburgh in 1990.{{r|goodbye}}

In the mid-1990s, she became one of the founders and leaders of the Risk Analysis Section of the [[American Statistical Association]],{{r|risk}} and one of its early chairs;{{r|risk2}} she also served as secretary–treasurer for the [[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies]].{{r|copss}} She left academia to become a statistical consultant in [[Washington, DC]] in 2014.{{r|goodbye}}

==Recognition==
Weissfeld was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1999.{{r|fasa}}

==Personal life==
Weissfeld is married to Joel Weissfeld, an [[Epidemiology|epidemiologist]].{{r|goodbye}}
